([[Bradenton, Florida]]) | college = [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2020–2021) | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2020]]) | medal_templates = }} '''Jaden Tyree Springer''' (born September 25, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. ==Early life and high school career== While in eighth grade, Springer played [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for Lighthouse Christian School in [[Antioch, Tennessee]], averaging a team-high 19 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Wertz Jr. |first1=Langston |title=One of the nation's highest-ranked freshman, Jaden Springer, to play basketball at Rocky River High |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article94969892.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=May 3, 2020 |date=August 10, 2016}} In his first two years of high school, he played for [[Rocky River High School (North Carolina)|Rocky River High School]] in [[Mint Hill, North Carolina]], being drawn by head basketball coach Jermaine Walker despite academic and disciplinary concerns about the school.{{cite web |last1=McLamb |first1=Michael |title=The Jaden Springer story: 'A quiet revelation' |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/jaden-springer-story-quiet-revelation |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=May 2, 2020 |date=June 4, 2018}} In his freshman season, Springer averaged 21.8 points, 9.4 rebounds and five assists per game and led his team to its first state tournament appearance.{{cite web |title=Jaden Springer |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/springer-jaden.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |access-date=May 3, 2020 |date=December 4, 2019}} As a sophomore, he averaged 24.7 points, 10.2 rebounds, 2.4 steals and 2.4 blocks per game, helping Rocky River reach the Class 4A state semifinals.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/yL1wLxRGiUeRCLlOOrsePA/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 3, 2020 |date=April 17, 2018}} He was named Southwestern 4A Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Wertz Jr. |first1=Langston |title=Jaden Springer, Nia Daniel named Southwestern 4A players of the year |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article202294184.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=May 4, 2020 |date=February 26, 2018}} Entering his junior and senior seasons, Springer transferred to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].{{cite web|title=Chosen 25 guard Jaden Springer transferring to IMG Academy|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2018/chosen-25-guard-jaden-springer-transferring-to-img-academy|website=[[USA Today]]|last=Jordan|first=Jason|date=August 22, 2018|access-date=September 9, 2019}} He joined one of the best teams in the country and became teammates with top recruits [[Armando Bacot]], [[Josh Green (basketball)|Josh Green]] and [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]].{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=Preseason Top 25 High School Basketball Rankings: No. 3 IMG Academy |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/kuLyZ6fKt0OSz-qM2ktJLw/preseason-top-25-high-school-basketball-rankings--no-3-img-academy.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 4, 2020 |date=October 17, 2018}} As a junior, Springer averaged 15.6 points, four rebounds and four assists, helping his team win [[High School Showcase|GEICO High School Nationals]].{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2018-19 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mdbwDYCSa02E7-TpRc5Gmg/maxpreps-2018-19-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 4, 2020 |date=April 11, 2019}} He scored 26 points in a 74–73 semifinal win over [[Montverde Academy]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=GEICO Nationals: No. 4 IMG Academy (Fla.) stages epic comeback to knockoff No. 3 Montverde (Fla.) Academy |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/geico-nationals-no-4-img-academy-fla-stages-epic-comeback-to-knockoff-no-3-montverde-fla-academy |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=May 4, 2020 |date=April 5, 2019}} In his senior season, Springer averaged 17.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game for IMG. He played through an ankle injury throughout the season and was in turn sidelined from some games.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2019-20 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/nm9MAVtXhkuj_dSz8iO6PA/maxpreps-2019-20-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 4, 2020 |date=March 25, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Ten Five-Star Prospects Make Montverde-IMG Must-See TV |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/cade-cunningham-scottie-barnes-montverde-jaden-springer-img-academy |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 4, 2020 |date=January 18, 2020}} Springer was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], which was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 30, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Springer began receiving scholarship offers from [[NCAA Division I]] basketball programs during his freshman season in high school.{{cite web |last1=Wertz Jr. |first1=Langston |title=Rocky River High freshman's talent dazzles coach, teammates, college recruiters |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article129043989.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=May 3, 2020 |date=January 26, 2017}} As a sophomore, he emerged as one of the best players in the 2020 class.{{cite web|title=How good is hotly recruited Jaden Springer? 'It's not fair,' Rocky River High coach says|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article200701309.html|website=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|last=Wertz Jr.|first=Langston|date=February 17, 2018|access-date=September 10, 2019}} On October 23, 2019, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] over offers from [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Rapp |first1=Timothy |title=5-Star SG Prospect Jaden Springer Commits to Tennessee over Memphis |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2840627-5-star-sg-prospect-jaden-springer-commits-to-tennessee-over-memphis |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] basketball|Tennessee Tech]].{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=Mike |title=Jaden Springer dazzles as Tennessee Vols basketball blows out Tennessee Tech |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2020/12/18/tennessee-vols-tennessee-tech-mens-basketball-updates-takeaways-score/6520529002/ Springer's father, [[Gary Springer|Gary]], was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] basketball player and played college basketball for [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]]. Gary was a sixth-round selection in the [[1984 NBA draft]] but did not play professionally due to a lingering knee injury. Both of Springer's older brothers played college basketball: Gary Jr. for Iona and Jordan for [[Army Black Knights men's basketball|Army]].
